doc: Quantile-map each row of `gen` onto Earth's distribution at its zone, interpolated linearly between zone centers: per zone present in both gen (zone of each gen row from _zone_index(lat_g, hadley)) and `ze`, a source table src = np.quantile(gen rows of the zone, QUANTILES) + k * 1e-9 and a destination table dst = np.quantile(earth rows with ze == z, QUANTILES) (linear method: virtual index (n - 1) q, lerp between the two neighbours, float64 even for float32 data; the float64 `+ arange * 1e-9` makes src strictly increasing); per row the two nearest zone centers (z + 0.5) * 5 around the row's Earth-equivalent latitude (np.searchsorted side left, minus 1, clipped), weight t = clip((el - c_i) / (c_j - c_i), 0, 1) (0 when only one zone is left or i == j), a = np.interp(row, src_i, dst_i) (clamps to dst[0] / dst[-1] outside the table, returns dst[j] exactly at a node, slope * (x - xp[j]) + fp[j] otherwise), b likewise for zone j (skipped when t == 0), out = a + t (b - a). The result has the dtype of `gen`. Tolerance: a port-style implementation (own sort-based quantile with the float64 lerp, an interp written as slope * (x - xp) + fp and as a lerp, float32 and float64 neighbour differences) differs from numpy by at most 6e-8 on the stored inputs (the float32 rounding of the stored output): the golden float32 tolerance. The function is NOT stable against its INPUTS: a one-ulp change of a gen texel that equals a plateau value of its zone (maps from bytes have many) moves that texel by up to 2.5e-4 through the 1e-9 ladder; hand it the exact stored inputs. Gen: the isotropic generated map at 64x32 (float32); earth: Earth at 128x64 (stored u8, / 255 in float32); ze as match_to_earth builds it (zones of the Earth rows at hadley 30, -1 beyond 67.5 degrees). Gen clipped to 0 and 1 (1.6 x - 0.3, clipped): long flat runs of exactly 0 and 1 in the quantiles, where the + 1e-9 k ladder is what keeps src strictly increasing (the interp then maps a texel equal to the plateau to dst of the plateau's first quantile). Input convention: the u8 input(s) earth are maps stored as bytes, and the function receives them as float32(u8) / float32(255) (`u8.astype(np.float32) / 255.0`: the division is done, and correctly rounded, in float32, as measure.load reads an 8-bit map), NOT as the raw bytes and NOT as a float64 quotient (a texel on a histogram edge or a threshold would move). params.u8_inputs lists them.

u8_inputs.earth: float32(u8) / float32(255), the division in float32
